I000001.name: Richard H. Ichord Jr.
I000001.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
I000001.bio: Richard H. Ichord Jr. was a Democratic U.S. Representative for Missouri's 8th congressional district (1961–1981). Ichord worked as a lawyer.

I000002.name: Santiago Iglesias
I000002.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
I000002.bio: Santiago Iglesias was a Coalitionist Resident Commissioner from Puerto Rico (1933–1939). Iglesias died in office in 1939.

I000003.name: James T. Igoe
I000003.photoCredit: Louis L. Emmerson (Illinois Secretary of State), author. Journal Printing Company (Springfield, Illinois), publisher., Public domain
I000003.bio: James T. Igoe was a Democratic U.S. Representative for Illinois's 6th congressional district (1927–1933). Igoe worked as a businessperson.

I000004.name: Michael L. Igoe
I000004.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
I000004.bio: Michael L. Igoe was a Democratic at-large U.S. Representative from Illinois (1935–1937). Igoe worked as a lawyer and judge.

I000005.name: William L. Igoe
I000005.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
I000005.bio: William L. Igoe was a Democratic U.S. Representative for Missouri's 11th congressional district (1913–1921). Igoe worked as a lawyer.

I000006.name: Peter Ihrie Jr.
I000006.bio: Peter Ihrie Jr. was a Jacksonian U.S. Representative for Pennsylvania's 8th congressional district (1829–1833). Ihrie worked as a lawyer.

I000007.name: Frank N. Ikard
I000007.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
I000007.bio: Frank N. Ikard was a Democratic U.S. Representative for Texas's 13th congressional district (1951–1961). Ikard worked as a lawyer and judge, served in the U.S. Army and was a veteran of World War II.

I000008.name: George P. Ikirt
I000008.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
I000008.bio: George P. Ikirt was a Democratic U.S. Representative for Ohio's 18th congressional district (1893–1895).

I000009.name: Daniel Ilsley
I000009.bio: Daniel Ilsley was a Democratic-Republican U.S. Representative for Massachusetts's 15th congressional district (1807–1809). Ilsley served in the U.S. Army.

I000010.name: Lawrence E. Imhoff
I000010.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
I000010.bio: Lawrence E. Imhoff was a Democratic U.S. Representative for Ohio's 18th congressional district (1933–1939, 1941–1943). Imhoff worked as a lawyer, served in the U.S. Navy and Marine Corps and was a veteran of World War I and World War II.

I000011.name: James H. Imlay
I000011.bio: James H. Imlay was a Federalist U.S. Representative from New Jersey (1797–1801). Imlay worked as a lawyer and educator.

I000012.name: John J. Ingalls
I000012.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
I000012.bio: John J. Ingalls was a Republican U.S. Senator from Kansas (1873–1891). Ingalls also served as President pro tempore of the Senate. Ingalls worked as a lawyer.

I000013.name: Samuel Williams Inge
I000013.bio: Samuel Williams Inge was a Democratic U.S. Representative for Alabama's 4th congressional district (1847–1851). Inge worked as a lawyer.

I000014.name: William Marshall Inge
I000014.bio: William Marshall Inge was a Jacksonian U.S. Representative for Tennessee's 10th congressional district (1833–1835). Inge worked as a lawyer.

I000015.name: Charles Jared Ingersoll
I000015.bio: Charles Jared Ingersoll was a U.S. Representative from Pennsylvania (1813–1815, 1841–1849), changing party over time (Democratic-Republican, then Democrat). Ingersoll worked as a lawyer.

I000016.name: Colin M. Ingersoll
I000016.bio: Colin M. Ingersoll was a Democratic U.S. Representative for Connecticut's 2nd congressional district (1851–1855). Ingersoll worked as a lawyer.

I000017.name: Ebon C. Ingersoll
I000017.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
I000017.bio: Ebon C. Ingersoll was a Republican U.S. Representative for Illinois's 5th congressional district (1864–1871). Ingersoll worked as a lawyer.

I000019.name: Joseph Reed Ingersoll
I000019.bio: Joseph Reed Ingersoll was a Whig U.S. Representative for Pennsylvania's 2nd congressional district (1835–1837, 1843–1849). Ingersoll worked as a lawyer and diplomat.

I000020.name: Ralph I. Ingersoll
I000020.bio: Ralph I. Ingersoll was an Adams at-large U.S. Representative from Connecticut (1825–1833). Ingersoll worked as a lawyer and judge.

I000021.name: Samuel Ingham
I000021.bio: Samuel Ingham was a U.S. Representative from Connecticut (1835–1839), changing party over time (Jacksonian, then Democrat). Ingham worked as a lawyer and judge.

I000022.name: Samuel D. Ingham
I000022.bio: Samuel D. Ingham was a U.S. Representative from Pennsylvania (1813–1818, 1822–1823, 1824, 1825–1831), changing party over time (Democratic-Republican, then Jackson Republican, then Jacksonian). Ingham also served as Secretary of the Treasury (1829–1831). Ingham worked as a businessperson.

I000023.name: Bob Inglis
I000023.photoCredit: U.S. Government Publishing Office / unitedstates project, Public domain (U.S. government work)
I000023.bio: Bob Inglis was a Republican U.S. Representative for South Carolina's 4th congressional district (1993–1999, 2005–2011). Inglis worked as a lawyer.

I000024.name: James M. Inhofe
I000024.photoCredit: U.S. Government Publishing Office / unitedstates project, Public domain (U.S. government work)
I000024.bio: James M. Inhofe was a Republican politician from Oklahoma who served as U.S. Representative (1987–1994) and U.S. Senator (1994–2023). Inhofe worked as a businessperson and aviator and served in the U.S. Army.

I000025.name: Daniel K. Inouye
I000025.photoCredit: U.S. Government Publishing Office / unitedstates project, Public domain (U.S. government work)
I000025.bio: Daniel K. Inouye was a Democratic politician from Hawaii who served as territorial Delegate (1959–1963) and U.S. Senator (1963–2012). Inouye also served as President pro tempore of the Senate. Inouye died in office in 2012.

I000026.name: Jay Inslee
I000026.photoCredit: U.S. Government Publishing Office / unitedstates project, Public domain (U.S. government work)
I000026.bio: Jay Inslee was a Democratic politician from Washington who served as U.S. Representative (1993–1995, 1999–2012) and Governor of Washington (2013–2025). Inslee worked as a lawyer and businessperson.

I000027.name: John L. M. Irby
I000027.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
I000027.bio: John L. M. Irby was a Democratic U.S. Senator from South Carolina (1891–1897). Irby worked as a lawyer.

I000028.name: James Iredell Jr.
I000028.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
I000028.bio: James Iredell Jr. was a Jacksonian politician from North Carolina who served as Governor of North Carolina (1827–1828) and U.S. Senator (1828–1831). Iredell worked as a lawyer and judge.

I000029.name: Andy Ireland
I000029.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
I000029.bio: Andy Ireland was a U.S. Representative from Florida (1977–1993), changing party over time (Democrat, then Republican). Ireland worked as a businessperson and diplomat.

I000030.name: Clifford C. Ireland
I000030.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
I000030.bio: Clifford C. Ireland was a Republican U.S. Representative for Illinois's 16th congressional district (1917–1923). Ireland worked as a lawyer.

I000031.name: Alfred Briggs Irion
I000031.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
I000031.bio: Alfred Briggs Irion was a Democratic U.S. Representative for Louisiana's 6th congressional district (1885–1887). Irion worked as a lawyer and journalist.

I000032.name: Alexander Irvin
I000032.bio: Alexander Irvin was a Whig U.S. Representative for Pennsylvania's 24th congressional district (1847–1849).

I000033.name: James Irvin
I000033.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
I000033.bio: James Irvin was a Whig U.S. Representative from Pennsylvania (1841–1845).

I000034.name: William W. Irvin
I000034.bio: William W. Irvin was a Jacksonian U.S. Representative for Ohio's 9th congressional district (1829–1833). Irvin worked as a lawyer and judge.

I000035.name: William Irvine
I000035.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
I000035.bio: William Irvine was an at-large U.S. Representative from Pennsylvania (1793–1795). Irvine worked as a physician, served in the U.S. Army and was a veteran of the Revolutionary War.

I000036.name: William Irvine
I000036.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
I000036.bio: William Irvine was a Republican U.S. Representative for New York's 28th congressional district (1859–1861). Irvine worked as a lawyer, served in the U.S. Army and was a veteran of the Civil War.

I000037.name: Leonard Irving
I000037.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
I000037.bio: Leonard Irving was a Democratic U.S. Representative for Missouri's 4th congressional district (1949–1953).

I000038.name: William Irving
I000038.photoCredit: Historic Hudson Valley (Pocantico Hills, New York)., Public domain
I000038.bio: William Irving was a Democratic-Republican U.S. Representative for New York's 2nd congressional district (1814–1819). Irving worked as a businessperson.

I000039.name: Donald J. Irwin
I000039.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
I000039.bio: Donald J. Irwin was a Democratic U.S. Representative for Connecticut's 4th congressional district (1959–1961, 1965–1969). Irwin worked as a lawyer and served in the U.S. Army.

I000040.name: Edward M. Irwin
I000040.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
I000040.bio: Edward M. Irwin was a Republican U.S. Representative for Illinois's 22nd congressional district (1925–1931).

I000041.name: Harvey Samuel Irwin
I000041.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
I000041.bio: Harvey Samuel Irwin was a Republican U.S. Representative for Kentucky's 5th congressional district (1901–1903). Irwin worked as a lawyer, served in the U.S. Army and was a veteran of the Civil War.

I000042.name: Jared Irwin
I000042.bio: Jared Irwin was a Democratic-Republican U.S. Representative for Pennsylvania's 10th congressional district (1813–1817). Irwin was a veteran of the War of 1812.

I000043.name: Thomas Irwin
I000043.photoCredit: United States District Court for the Western District of Pennsylvania, Public domain
I000043.bio: Thomas Irwin was a Jacksonian U.S. Representative for Pennsylvania's 14th congressional district (1829–1831). Irwin worked as a lawyer and judge.

I000044.name: William W. Irwin
I000044.bio: William W. Irwin was a Whig U.S. Representative for Pennsylvania's 22nd congressional district (1841–1843). Irwin worked as a diplomat.

I000045.name: Jacob C. Isacks
I000045.bio: Jacob C. Isacks was a U.S. Representative for Tennessee's 4th congressional district (1823–1833), changing party over time (Jackson Republican, then Jacksonian).

I000046.name: Leo Isacson
I000046.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
I000046.bio: Leo Isacson was an American Labor U.S. Representative for New York's 24th congressional district (1948–1949). Isacson worked as a lawyer and educator.

I000047.name: Ernest Istook
I000047.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
I000047.bio: Ernest Istook was a Republican U.S. Representative for Oklahoma's 5th congressional district (1993–2007). Istook worked as a lawyer and journalist.

I000048.name: Anthony F. Ittner
I000048.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
I000048.bio: Anthony F. Ittner was a Republican U.S. Representative for Missouri's 1st congressional district (1877–1879). Ittner worked as a businessperson.

I000049.name: Alfred Iverson Sr.
I000049.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
I000049.bio: Alfred Iverson Sr. was a Democratic politician from Georgia who served as U.S. Representative (1847–1849) and U.S. Senator (1855–1861). Iverson worked as a lawyer and judge.

I000050.name: Irving Ives
I000050.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
I000050.bio: Irving Ives was a Republican U.S. Senator from New York (1947–1959). Ives worked as an educator, served in the U.S. Army and was a veteran of World War I.

I000051.name: Willard Ives
I000051.photoCredit: John A Haddock, editor., Public domain
I000051.bio: Willard Ives was a Democratic U.S. Representative for New York's 19th congressional district (1851–1853).

I000052.name: Edouard Izac
I000052.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
I000052.bio: Edouard Izac was a Democratic U.S. Representative from California (1937–1947). Izac served in the U.S. Navy, was a veteran of World War I and received the Medal of Honor.

I000053.name: Ralph Izard
I000053.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
I000053.bio: Ralph Izard was a Pro-Administration U.S. Senator from South Carolina (1789–1795). Izard also served as President pro tempore of the Senate.

I000054.name: James F. Izlar
I000054.bio: James F. Izlar was a Democratic U.S. Representative for South Carolina's 1st congressional district (1894–1895). Izlar worked as a lawyer and judge.

I000055.name: Johnny Isakson
I000055.photoCredit: U.S. Government Publishing Office / unitedstates project, Public domain (U.S. government work)
I000055.bio: Johnny Isakson was a Republican politician from Georgia who served as U.S. Representative (1999–2005) and U.S. Senator (2005–2019). Isakson worked as a businessperson and economist and served in the U.S. Air Force.

I000056.name: Darrell Issa
I000056.photoCredit: U.S. Government Publishing Office / unitedstates project, Public domain (U.S. government work)
I000056.bio: Darrell Issa is a Republican U.S. Representative from California (2001–2019, since 2021). Issa worked as a businessperson and served in the U.S. Army.

I000057.name: Steve Israel
I000057.photoCredit: U.S. Government Publishing Office / unitedstates project, Public domain (U.S. government work)
I000057.bio: Steve Israel was a Democratic U.S. Representative from New York (2001–2017). Israel worked as an educator.

I000058.name: Glenn Ivey
I000058.photoCredit: U.S. Government Publishing Office / unitedstates project, Public domain (U.S. government work)
I000058.bio: Glenn Ivey is a Democratic U.S. Representative for Maryland's 4th congressional district, in office since 2023. Ivey worked as a lawyer.
